metadata.title: 2025 update to European Stroke Organisation (ESO) guideline on blood pressure management in acute ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage
top_takeaways: Routine pre-hospital blood pressure lowering in suspected stroke is advised against based on moderate-certainty evidence.

For AIS patients undergoing reperfusion therapy, strict blood pressure thresholds (< 185/110 mmHg pre-thrombolysis; < 180/105 mmHg during/after thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy) are recommended.
In acute intracerebral haemorrhage with small-to-moderate haematomas, early systolic blood pressure reduction to < 140 mmHg is supported to limit haematoma expansion.

recommendations.statement: We advise against routine pre-hospital blood pressure lowering in suspected stroke.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with suspected acute stroke in the pre-hospital setting
recommendations.verbatim_quote: We advise against routine pre-hospital blood pressure lowering in suspected stroke.

recommendations.statement: In AIS patients undergoing reperfusion therapy, we recommend maintaining blood pressure < 185/110 mmHg before the bolus of intravenous thrombolysis and < 180/105 mmHg during and for 24 h after intravenous thrombolysis and/or mechanical thrombectomy.
recommendations.target_population: Acute ischaemic stroke patients undergoing intravenous thrombolysis or mechanical thrombectomy
